subject: Ownership handoff & capacity rebalance — QBR alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, Mar 20, 2028 at 9:15 AM PDT
Subject: Ownership handoff & capacity rebalance — QBR alignment

Team —

Sharing an initial proposal for ownership handoffs and a short capacity rebalance ahead of the ArcadiaHealth QBR. Goal is to tighten account coverage, simplify escalation paths, and make the QBR narrative cleaner for the exec review. Attachments: ownership-map.xlsx (coverage matrix) and qbr-slide-deck-v1.pptx (draft for internal review).

High-level changes I propose:
- Move primary TAM ownership for ArcadiaHealth from LA to Jonas (operational continuity + platform expertise).
- Re-route Tier-1 oncall and billing escalation to a single point (Neha) for next 90 days while we stabilize throughput.
- Temporarily increase dedicated capacity allocation for their key workloads by 20% for six weeks to address latency spikes observed in Feb.

Asks:
1) Quick pass on the ownership-map.xlsx (highlight any redlines).
2) Jonas — confirm you can take TAM lead and whether we should reassign any direct reports.
3) Laura — I'll need a short comms paragraph for the broader CS+Sales org and a timeline for the announcement.
4) Please review the deck slides and give feedback by EOD Wednesday so we can share with execs before Friday's QBR dry run.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ownership-map.xlsx (14KB), qbr-slide-deck-v1.pptx (2.4MB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

> Sharing an initial proposal for ownership handoffs and a short capacity rebalance ahead of the ArcadiaHealth QBR...

Thanks Ben — good start. Two quick items from my side:

1) Timeline: I suggest we wait one week before public comms to the broader customer base. Instead, share the change with ArcadiaHealth and CS leads, then announce internally after exec sign-off.
2) Coverage: moving TAM to Jonas makes sense operationally, but we should keep a named secondary (L2) owner for escalation continuity. I propose we keep Grace as the secondary until the end of Q2.

I attached a brief "comm-draft.docx" with a proposed internal paragraph and a short customer-facing blurb. Also flagged one slide in the deck (slide 7) where the capacity numbers should be clarified — the 20% bump needs the exact VM profile called out.

If Jonas can confirm by midday, I'll prep a one-paragraph announcer for exec review.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

I can take primary TAM ownership for ArcadiaHealth. Quick notes from Ops side:
- I'll keep the current TPM (Maya) on as day-to-day contact for infra/throughput items to preserve institutional knowledge.
- Proposed timeline for internal communications:
   - Wed (tomorrow): share updated ownership map with Execs for 24-hr review.
   - Fri: internal CS+Sales announcement (post-exec sign-off).
   - Mon next week: customer comms live (coordinated with Ben/Laura).

Draft internal comms paragraph (feel free to copy):
"As part of our QBR readiness and to improve operational accountability, ArcadiaHealth will move to a single TAM lead (Jonas Weber) with continued support from the existing TPM. This will simplify escalation paths and provide clearer ownership during the upcoming capacity stabilization window."

I'll also sync with Infra on the 20% capacity bump to confirm cost/spot implications; if there's a major cost delta we should present options.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Liu <anna@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, Mar 22, 2028 at 8:00 AM PDT
Subject: ArcadiaHealth QBR — proposed ownership changes & capacity plan

Anna —

Following up on our QBR prep: we are proposing a short-term ownership and capacity rebalance to make the coming QBR simple and to address the latency spikes you reported in February. Key points: 

- Jonas Weber will be your primary TAM for the upcoming QBR cycle; Laura and I will remain involved for escalation and commercial context.
- We propose a temporary 20% capacity increase (same VM class) for six weeks to smooth peak windows while the infra changes are validated.
- We will present an updated QBR deck that outlines expected impact and timelines (attached).

We'd like to present this in the QBR on Friday. Can we confirm a 30-minute slot at 10:00 AM PT that day, or alternatively 2:00 PM PT? If either works I'll send a calendar invite and the final deck.

Thanks for flagging the latency items — Jonas and his team will prioritize root-cause analysis after we align on the short-term capacity move.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr-slide-deck-v1.pptx (2.4MB)
Shared link: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=1a2BqQBRDeck

Thanks all —

Confirming the plan and next steps from a leadership comms perspective:

Action items:
- Ben: finalize deck and circulate to Execs (JZ, MK) for sign-off by Thu 12:00 PM PT.
- Laura: finalize the internal announcement and ensure CS leads have the L2 contact (Grace) listed.
- Jonas: confirm infra cost delta for the 20% bump and whether we need a billing credit ask.
- I'll draft a short executive note for JZ and MK that highlights the risk mitigation and expected customer impact.

If we hit these items on Thursday, we can run the dry QBR Friday and take to ArcadiaHealth same day. I'll escalate if execs ask for additional details.

Neha Kapoor
